newsitem.title: KUWAIT: Kuwait arrests suspects after attack on MP - sources.
newsitem.headline: Kuwait arrests suspects after attack on MP - sources.

text.p: Kuwait has arrested suspects in connection with an attempt to kill a leading liberal opposition parliamentarian, political sources said on Sunday.

The sources said police were questioning at least three people suspected of links to the Friday evening attempt against Oxford-educated Abdullah al-Naibari, 61, who was shot twice. His wife was also wounded when their car was sprayed with bullets.
Local newspapers on Sunday had various reports on arrest of suspects, including non-Kuwaitis, but there was no official confirmation.

Political and diplomatic sources said one of those arrested appeared to be a Kuwaiti national who was the target of several recent reports by Talea weekly, the mouthpiece of Naibari's political grouping.
"Talea has reported on many alleged wrong-doings in the past few months, attacking various personalities and groups. They have made quite a few enemies," said a European diplomat.
MPs have accused what they call "public funds thieves" of being behind the attack.
"The main suspect in question now is said to have been a middleman for government contracts. He had a few dealings with arms deals," said a Western diplomat.

In December Kuwait said it had eliminated middlemen from arms purchases to cut costs. MPs have criticised large commissions for brokers in multi-billion-dollar arms deals and have opened several inquiries in alleged irregularities.
Naibari has played a key role in efforts to combat alleged corruption since parliament was restored in 1992 and he often questions lucrative arms deals.
Sea captain Abdul-Rahman Naibari told Reuters on Sunday that his brother is in "very good condition" in hospital. "He is talking and we read him the newspapers."

Gunmen ambushed Naibari's car as he drove to Kuwait City from a beach near the southern border with Saudi Arabia. He was hit in the jaw and shoulder and his wife suffered a superficial bullet wound near her left shoulder.

The Kuwait News Agency KUNA said the Emir, Sheikh Jaber al-Ahmad al-Sabah, had ordered that Naibari be sent abroad for treatment and the Ministry of Health was making arrangements for him to leave by the end of the week.
